Done. Here's what I built and verified.

## Files created

| File | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `index.html` | The whole app — markup, CSS and JS in one dependency-free file (695 lines) |
| `README.md` | How to run it, feature notes, storage format, how to run the tests |

## How to run

```sh
cd /private/tmp/.../scratchpad/d-code-1/work/apps
python3 -m http.server 8000   # then open http://localhost:8000/
```
Double-clicking `index.html` also works, but serving over HTTP guarantees `localStorage` is available in every browser (the app detects a blocked store and shows a warning banner rather than silently losing data).

## Requirements → implementation

- **Add habits** — form at the top (`maxlength=60`, trims whitespace, ignores blank/whitespace-only input, keeps focus so you can add several in a row).
- **Tick off today** — big toggle button per card ("Mark done for today" ⇄ "✓ Done today — tap to undo"). The card border and chip turn green when today is done.
- **Last 7 days per habit** — a 7-column grid, oldest → newest, today outlined and labelled; each cell is a button showing the weekday letter + day number, pressed-in/green when done. Clicking a past day corrects it (also gives you the "I forgot yesterday" case).
- **Streak count** — blue chip: consecutive completed days ending today, or ending yesterday if today isn't ticked yet (so the streak isn't killed by a day you haven't gotten to yet). Plus a "Best N" chip and an "N/7 this week" chip.
- **Remember everything** — saved to `localStorage` under `habit-tracker.v1` on every mutation; reloaded and re-rendered on return; `storage` events keep multiple tabs in sync; a 60-second timer re-renders when the calendar day rolls over in an open tab.
- **Delete a habit** — the ✕ per card, with a confirmation prompt, then focus returns to the input.

## Correctness details worth knowing

- Date keys are built from **local** calendar parts (`YYYY-MM-DD`), never `toISOString()`, so an 11pm tick stays on that day and `addDays` is DST-safe.
- `isValidDateKey` round-trips through `Date`, so junk like `2026-13-01` or `2026-02-31` in storage can't create a phantom day; malformed habits/entries are filtered on load instead of crashing.
- User text is rendered with `textContent` / `<template>` cloning — no `innerHTML`, so habit names can't inject markup.
- Accessibility: labelled controls, `aria-pressed` on toggles, descriptive `aria-label`s per day ("Thursday, 29 Oct — done, tap to undo"), focus preserved across re-render, and a light/dark theme via `prefers-color-scheme`.

## Validation

I don't have a shell/browser in this environment, so I couldn't execute the page myself. Instead I reviewed the full file line by line (balanced IIFE/braces, no leftover build markers, no stale `isDateKey` references) and added an **in-app test runner**: open `index.html#selftest` and it prints 30 checks — date-key padding, DST and year-boundary arithmetic, `isNextDay`, key validation, all six streak edge cases, the 7-day window boundary, corrupt-data repair, and a `localStorage` round-trip using a scratch key — plus a `N/N checks passed` line in a panel and the console. The tests use throwaway fixtures, so your saved habits are untouched.
